features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: Captures the level of formal technical education the applicant cites as relevant preparation.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience only, with no advanced degree presented.
Master's degree in computer science or a related field is presented.
Doctoral degree in computer science or a related field is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems architecture
features.description: Captures hands-on design ownership of agent-based systems, especially their control boundaries, guardrails, and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: No agentic systems experience is mentioned.
References agents in passing without clear ownership or design detail.
Describes a concrete agentic pipeline or tooling example.
Shows end-to-end ownership of agentic architecture, including boundaries, supervision, permissions, logging, or auditability.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering work.

levels.descriptor: No algorithmic strength is mentioned.
Claims strong data-structure or algorithm knowledge, but without a concrete example.
Gives at least one concrete example of improving a system through better algorithm or data-structure choice.
Uses a specific, nontrivial example to show strong algorithmic judgment and a meaningful systems improvement.

features.name: Applied AI production maturity
features.description: Captures real production experience deploying AI systems, especially with reliability, evaluation, hardening, or failure-mode awareness.

levels.descriptor: No AI evidence.
Only vague, aspirational, or lightly specified AI mention.
Shows concrete experience shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality.
Shows concrete production AI work plus explicit evaluation, guardrails, correctness, or failure-mode management.

features.name: Collaboration and learning posture
features.description: Captures coachability, willingness to partner with security specialists, and a collaborative approach to learning and building.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention collaboration with security partners.
Implies support for other engineers, but not specifically partnership with security specialists.
Explicitly states readiness to work with security engineers or build for their workflows.
Shows explicit partnership mindset plus concrete evidence of learning from, serving, or collaborating with security specialists.

features.name: Developer enablement mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security engineering as helping developers succeed through secure defaults, lower friction, and user-centered tooling.

levels.descriptor: Does not discuss the needs or behavior of developer users.
Mentions helping teams in generic terms.
Explicitly focuses on reducing friction or making the secure path easier for developers.
Shows clear empathy for busy engineers and explains adoption in terms of defaults, workflows, and usable tooling rather than process.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how consistently the letter substantiates claims with concrete examples, mechanisms, named systems, or implementation detail.

levels.descriptor: Relies mostly on broad claims with little supporting detail.
Names some relevant work but gives limited mechanism or outcome detail.
Provides clear examples of work with enough detail to judge fit.
Provides multiple specific examples tied to mechanisms, tradeoffs, or outcomes.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how central and production-grade the applicant's Go experience appears.

levels.descriptor: Go is merely listed or mentioned in passing.
Go is named as a main language, but without role-shaped examples.
Go is presented as a primary production language for backend or systems work.
Shows strong Go ownership tied directly to relevant systems such as backends, guardrails, or operated services.

features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter explains the visible outcomes or operational effects of the applicant's work.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on broad claims of fit, skill, or interest without outcomes.
The letter gives some concrete examples of work, but the effect on users, systems, or teams is unclear.
The letter ties accomplishments to visible improvements, such as faster systems, cleaner queues, or reduced manual work.
The letter gives specific accomplishments plus clear operational or organizational outcomes, ideally quantified or sharply contrasted with the prior state.

features.name: Maintainer mindset
features.description: Captures whether the applicant emphasizes maintainability, operability, reliability, failure-awareness, and long-term ownership over feature shipping alone.

levels.descriptor: Shows no explicit maintainability or reliability orientation.
Implies care for quality but not as a recurring theme.
Clearly values maintainable, dependable systems or draws on maintenance experience.
Makes long-term operability a central lens, emphasizing inheritance, quiet resilience, or higher standards for security-critical software.

features.name: Narrative coherence and distinctiveness
features.description: Captures whether the letter presents a memorable, coherent, well-shaped story rather than a disconnected or generic list of qualifications.

levels.descriptor: The letter reads like an interchangeable template or a flat list of qualifications.
The letter is competent but generic, with limited individuality in framing or voice.
The letter has a distinctive opening, viewpoint, or sustained framing device.
The letter is memorable and cohesive, with a clear throughline linking the opening idea, past work, and motivation for this role.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing hands-on adversarial security practice outside ordinary development work, such as CTF participation.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-security practice is mentioned.
Shows occasional or casual participation in CTFs or similar practice.
Shows sustained participation in CTFs or other regular adversarial practice.
Shows sustained adversarial practice with strong competitive results or clearly serious investment.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures responsibility for public code through upstream fixes, contributions, maintainership, releases, or other external accountability.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or fixes.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a small project or recurring upstream responsibility.
The letter shows sustained stewardship of an open-source project with users, releases, reviews, or community responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and relevance of self-directed projects described outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No personal project is mentioned.
Mentions a small utility or light side project with modest technical scope.
Describes a substantive side project with meaningful systems or infrastructure work.
Describes an ambitious self-directed systems project tackling distributed correctness, recovery, delivery guarantees, or similarly hard engineering problems.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation toward foundational infrastructure work whose benefits compound across many teams or systems.

levels.descriptor: Does not show any particular interest in foundational or shared systems work.
Mentions scale or impact in passing, but not as a central motivation.
Explicitly values platform or infrastructure work because it benefits many teams.
Persuasively frames central tooling as a multiplier, emphasizing inherited impact or organization-wide capacity gains.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: Captures the amount, breadth, and ownership depth of professional experience shipping, operating, and maintaining production software.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Programming language breadth
features.description: Captures the range of programming languages or technical versatility the letter shows beyond the core required language.

levels.descriptor: Only Go is mentioned, or language breadth is unclear.
Shows Go plus one or two additional languages.
Shows Go plus several additional languages.
Shows Go plus broad multi-language experience across many systems.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how substantial, concrete, and production-oriented the applicant's Python experience appears.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or only minimally mentioned.
Python is mentioned for light scripting or general familiarity.
Python is used regularly for tooling, automation, analysis, or services.
Python is presented as production-grade and central, with evidence of robust service or tooling development.

features.name: Role-specific mission fit
features.description: Captures how specifically the letter understands this exact security-automation role and maps the applicant's motivation and background to its mission and responsibilities.

levels.descriptor: The letter shows little understanding of the specific security problem this team solves.
The letter shows general interest in security engineering, but mostly at a broad level.
The letter clearly articulates goals like reducing manual security work or making the secure path easier for developers.
The letter shows nuanced insight into bottlenecks such as scarce expert attention, vulnerability triage, lifecycle embedding, bounded agents, or similar operational realities.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on experience performing security reviews or assessments such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface analysis, or fix validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the presence and rigor of formal third-party security credentials cited as evidence of security knowledge or skill.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A baseline credential such as Security+ is presented.
A hands-on offensive credential such as OSCP is presented.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful, rigorous view of security engineering and a serious commitment to security-hardening work.

levels.descriptor: Offers no distinct philosophy about the quality bar required for security engineering.
Makes only generic statements about reliability or security importance.
Expresses a clear philosophy of quiet resilience, dependable systems, or a higher standard for security tooling.
Builds a memorable, well-integrated case that security tooling demands exceptional rigor and ties that belief to prior work or design choices.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience building tooling that automates vulnerability intake, classification, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or similar response workflows.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not describe vulnerability-handling automation.
The letter mentions security automation in general, but not a specific vulnerability triage workflow.
The letter shows direct experience automating intake, classification, routing, or deduplication of vulnerability reports.
The letter shows a clear transformation of a manual vulnerability workflow or explicitly states operational impact from the automation.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures the surface-level mechanical quality of the prose, including proofreading, spelling, grammar, and sentence-level care.

levels.descriptor: Frequent errors repeatedly interrupt reading or seriously undermine credibility.
Noticeable proofreading problems distract the reader more than once.
Contains some typos, but the letter remains easy to follow.
Mostly clean, with at most a minor slip.
Polished and effectively error-free at a professional standard.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic dimensions that do not clearly belong to any broader recurring construct.

levels.descriptor: Does not address how security work should interact with developer workflows.
Expresses a general desire to help teams, but without a clear enablement philosophy.
Explicitly emphasizes secure defaults, reduced friction, or assisting engineers rather than adding process.
Shows a strong developer-enablement philosophy and backs it with language or examples of tooling that removed burden from engineers.
